messages:
maya: heads up — noticed a weird cost spike for customer 'borealis' on the token dashboard. between 11:02-11:07 UTC a bunch of streaming sessions show duplicate 'credit_ticker' entries :eyes:
jon: link? which view /model or /session?
maya: /console/customers/borealis/usage -> timeline + token-metering. spike aligns with router deploy at ~11:05 (ops-bot shows canary).
alex: I pulled raw logs. looks like the router retried resume flows and the ledger accepted both resume events because the kv-tag on the session was missing/stale. snippet:
```
2026-03-23T11:04:59Z router=router-3 session=abc123 resume_attempt=1 kv_tag=kv:stale_0x9c9
2026-03-23T11:05:02Z router=router-3 session=abc123 resume_attempt=2 kv_tag=kv:stale_0x9c9
2026-03-23T11:05:03Z ledger=ledger-2 emit_credit customer=borealis amount=12 tag=kv:stale_0x9c9
2026-03-23T11:05:03Z ledger=ledger-2 emit_credit customer=borealis amount=12 tag=kv:stale_0x9c9
```
lena: that double emit is the problem. ledger currently dedupes by (session_id, op_id) but resume retries had different op_id so both applied.
cassie: is the UX showing duplicate lines or aggregated? product wants to know if customers see two charges.
maya: console shows two separate ledger events on the timeline and the billing pipeline later aggregated into two micro-charges. so yes, visible in per-request drilldown.
jon: quick mitigation options: 1) patch ledger to dedupe on kv_tag if present, 2) make router sticky with resume backoff to avoid duplicate resumes, 3) console can hide duplicate adjacent emits temporarily to reduce churn. which move is lowest-risk?
alex: option 3 is low-risk but doesn't fix billing. option 1 is risky because kv_tag can be legitimately reused across sessions in some paths. option 2 seems safe and small: add a 500ms jitter/backoff on resume attempts for canaryed router.
lena: I worry about race windows: the root cause might be stale sidecar state that reissued resume with an old kv tag that other components treat as canonical. we should add producer-side guard: include resume_nonce in emit so ledger can ignore retried resumes with same nonce.
cassie: timeline for fixes? ops wants a quick rollback if we can't contain refunds.
ops-bot: Deploy 2026-03-23T11:05:10Z router/v2.1 -> canary-10%
jon: Can we run a targeted reconcile for borealis to refund obvious duplicates? alex, can you write a query to detect back-to-back identical emits (within 1s) with same tag and amount?
alex: yes, will post query now and run on ledger events.
alex: query result sample: 7 candidate duplicate groups in 11:02-11:08 window for borealis. total ~84 tokens credited extra.
maya: thanks. request: add a dashboard alert rule for sudden adjacent-emit ratio > 0.2 for any customer, and surface the router deploy/rollout id in the incident link. that will speed detection next time. :thumbsup:
jon: agree. owner: eng-platform (me) for rollout-backoff patch; eng-runtime (lena) for nonce guard proposal; product (cassie) for dashboard alert wording.
lena: i'll prototype resume_nonce header and a ledger config flag to honor it. low-risk toggle.
cassie: I'll update billing FAQ and send a short customer note for borealis after reconcile.
maya: temporary action: alex to run reconcile job, jon to gate router rollout to pause at 0% until backoff patch is in canary.
jon: paused canary. setting rollout to manual.
alex: reconcile job queued -> run id r-20260323-01. I'll post results once finished.
maya: perfect. follow-up thread for postmortem after reconcile. thanks all. :pray:
